name: fire_element_small_loop
drive_hint: tap(sim.terminals[:1], amplitude=1.0, burst_len=24) or repeated_taps at period=8 steps (f0=1/8=0.125 cyc/sample)
notes: r=5px loop, circumference ~31.4px, length_samples=8, f0=0.125 cyc/sample -- lands between band3 (0.0915) and band4 (0.1913) of the 6 log-spaced filterbank bands. Measured kinetic-weighted vs thermal-weighted peak band energy ratio kin/therm=0.10 (thermal ~10x kinetic): reads clearly as a 'fire' element. r=5 is close to the small-radius edge of the loop-closure-safe zone (r>=~4.5px with default n=48/tail=40) -- see bug 'loop-closure-fragility' before shrinking further.

name: kinetic_element_large_loop
drive_hint: tap(sim.terminals[:1], amplitude=1.0, burst_len=24) or repeated_taps at period=126 steps (f0=1/126=0.00794 cyc/sample)
notes: r=80px loop, circumference ~502.7px, length_samples=126, f0=0.00794 cyc/sample -- sits just below band0 (0.01) and well below every other band. Measured kin/therm peak-band-energy ratio = 4.82: reads clearly as a kinetic/force element. r=63.7px (length_samples=100) lands f0 exactly on band0's center (0.01) and is an equally clean 'pure kinetic' reference size.

name: neutral_crossover_loop
notes: r=25px, f0=0.0256 cyc/sample, roughly between band1 (0.0209) and band2 (0.0437). Measured kin/therm ratio = 1.07 -- the size at which the element reads as neither clearly fire nor clearly force; useful as the boundary reference between the two other scenarios.

name: beat_two_loops_shared_junction
drive_hint: Find the two degree-3 loop-attach nodes (farthest from origin) and drive each with its own held_tone: held_tone([nodeA], frequency=0.007937, amplitude=0.4, attack_steps=400, duration_steps=7000) and held_tone([nodeB], frequency=0.007092, amplitude=0.4, attack_steps=400, duration_steps=7000) simultaneously (merge the two injection dicts per step). Observe sim.terminals[0] (the stub tip, the only true degree-1 terminal) via drives[term]['last_emitted'].
notes: rA=80px (f0A=0.007937, loop length 126 samples), rB=90px (f0B=0.007092, loop length 141 samples). Predicted beat period = 1/|f0A-f0B| = 1184 steps. Measured beat period from the combined terminal's envelope (carrier-smoothed |signal|): ~1195-1199 steps, within ~1% of prediction. Envelope swings between ~0.21 (near-cancellation) and ~1.10 (near-reinforcement) amplitude units riding on a much faster ~130-step carrier oscillation -- a clearly visible slow swell/fade distinct from the fast ringing.

name: rhythm_resonant_loop
drive_hint: Tap the loop-CLOSING junction node (the degree-3 node where tail meets loop), NOT the open terminal. repeated_taps([attach_node], period_steps=126, amplitude=0.8, burst_len=8, n_taps=20) for on-beat; repeated_taps([attach_node], period_steps=176, amplitude=0.8, burst_len=8, n_taps=20) for off-beat (period mismatched by 1.4x).
notes: r=80px, f0=0.007937, period_steps=126. With storage_ink (rad_admittance_fraction=0.1, lower damping than default), on-beat repeated tapping builds peak network_energy to ~2.3-2.7x a single tap's peak, saturating after only ~4 in-phase taps (driven-oscillator steady state). Off-beat (period x1.4 mismatch) reaches only ~1.4-2.1x over the same 20-30 taps and same total injected amplitude. IMPORTANT: tapping the open terminal directly (instead of the loop-closing junction) barely builds up at all (~1.8x even best-case) because the terminal's own Y_rad leak bleeds each burst straight back out -- injection site matters as much as timing for this mechanic to read as intended.

name: resonance_sharpness_loop
drive_hint: held_tone([attach_node], frequency=f, amplitude=0.05, attack_steps=800, duration_steps=4000) swept over f = f0*{0.75,0.86,0.90,0.92,0.94,0.96,1.0,1.06,1.1,1.2,1.3} where f0=0.007937; measure mean network_energy over the last 200-300 steps as the steady-state response at each f.
notes: True driven resonance peak sits at ~0.92*f0 (0.00730 cyc/sample), about 8% BELOW the nominal f0=1/length_samples=0.007937 used by the chirality/harmonic bookkeeping -- the tail+terminal boundary condition shifts the real resonance away from the idealized bare-loop circumference formula. Steady-state energy: 0.1331 at the true peak (0.92*f0), 0.0383 (29% of peak) at the nominal f0, 0.0504 (38%) at 0.86*f0, 0.0161 (12%) at 1.06*f0, 0.0111 (8%) at 0.75*f0. Estimated FWHM ~0.095 in relative-frequency units -> Q ~ 10-11: a clearly sharp, single-peaked resonance suitable for a resonant-shattering mechanic, but tuning puzzles should calibrate against the measured driven response, not the naive f0=c/L formula, or keep tails short relative to loop circumference to minimize the ~8% shift.

name: regression_loop_closure_fails_small_radius
notes: BUG: with default n=48, tail_length=40, a r=3px loop_with_tail_points shape FAILS TO CLOSE into a loop. The parser's self-intersection snap (point-proximity on the resampled+smoothed polyline) never detects that the loop's end coincides with its own start, so the whole stroke collapses into a single open two-terminal line (2 nodes, both degree 1, 0 self-loop edges) instead of a loop+tail (2 nodes: one degree-3 loop-closing junction + one degree-1 terminal). Result: no resonance, no chirality sign, no nonlinearity site -- the entire loop-based mechanic silently vanishes for a shape that looks like a valid tiny loop. Confirmed safe range with these defaults is roughly r in [4.5px, 90px]; increasing n does not fix the small-radius failure (tested n up to 500) because smoothing_window=5 in Stroke.resampled blurs across most or all of a very small loop's own circumference.

name: regression_loop_closure_fails_large_radius
drive_hint: Sim(strokes); inspect sim.graph.nodes / sim.terminals. Compare against the same shape built with n=72 or higher, which closes correctly.
notes: BUG: same closure-detection fragility as the small-radius case, opposite cause. With default n=48, a r>=~92px loop_with_tail_points shape also fails to close (2 open terminals, no self-loop edge) because larger radius means wider spacing between the loop's 48 polyline vertices, and the corner where tail meets loop gets smoothed (smoothing_window=5) further away from the true closure point than snap_eps=8px can catch. Raising n to 72+ fixes r=100 in testing. Fix direction: scale the loop's point count with radius (e.g. n proportional to circumference/dx) inside loop_with_tail_points, or shrink the smoothing window relative to local point spacing, or snap the stroke's own start/end point explicitly rather than relying on generic self-intersection detection for closed shapes.

name: regression_chirality_top_band_silently_zero
notes: BUG (same class as the already-fixed all-zero-for-no-loop bug, but a surviving second instance): compute_chirality's per-band gaussian harmonic-proximity weight underflows to numerical zero whenever a loop's fundamental times max_harmonic=8 doesn't get within roughly 3-4 sigma (sigma=0.03) of a band's center. For this r=63.7px loop (f0=0.01, 8th harmonic=0.08) band5 (center 0.4) is far outside that range, so total_weight<=1e-12 and chirality[5] falls back to the literal 0.0 in the 'else 0.0' branch -- even though the loop has a real, well-defined winding sign. Verified for r=25,40,63.7,80px (chirality[5]=0.0 in every case) while r=5,16px (whose harmonics do reach band5) get the correct signed value. Because THERMAL_BAND_WEIGHTS[5]=1.0 (the single heaviest thermal weight) and PHASE's heaviest weight also sits on band5, this silently zeroes the signed thermal (burn/chill) contribution from the top band -- and therefore a chunk of the 'ice is negative thermal coupling' mechanic -- for essentially every loop size at or above the 'neutral crossover' size (~r=25px) and up, i.e. for most kinetic-leaning loops. Suggested fix: raise max_harmonic and/or sigma so large, low-f0 loops still reach the top band(s), or fall back to sign-only-no-decay-to-zero (e.g. nearest-harmonic sign) instead of an explicit 0.0 when total_weight underflows.

name: regression_extreme_amplitude_bypasses_energy_ceiling_at_analyzer
drive_hint: tap(sim.terminals[:1], amplitude=1e6, burst_len=16); run ~1000 steps; inspect drives[term]['kinetic'] / ['bands'] per step alongside network_energy.
notes: BUG: the Sec.8 hard per-network energy ceiling (max_energy=50 default) correctly clamps the delay-line buffers within a few dozen steps (network_energy: 50 -> 1.65 -> 0.0000012 by step 500), but it clamps buffers only -- it does NOT rescale the SAME step's `radiated` return value or `node.last_emitted`, which is exactly what feeds the terminal FilterBank/analyzer. A single amplitude=1e6 tap therefore floods the analyzer with raw, unclamped multi-million-scale samples; the resulting kinetic-drive readout peaks above 3e10 and is still ~6e5 at step 500 and ~18 at step 1000, decaying only via the FilterBank's own slow leaky integrator (envelope_coef=0.05) long after the underlying wave simulation itself is already back near zero. A single bad/adversarial injection can therefore push kinetic/thermal/phase world-coupling many orders of magnitude out of scale for hundreds of steps even though the wave sim's own numerical stability mitigation is working exactly as designed. Suggested fix: clamp injected amplitude at the injection site, and/or apply the same energy-ratio scale factor computed in Network._clamp_energy to `radiated` and each terminal node's `last_emitted` before it reaches the analyzer, in the same step.
